framing.lineOfInquiry: Vikram Singh (P00036) may have been involved in the incident recorded in CASE032
framing.alternate: Vikram Singh (P00036) was not involved — the evidence has an innocent explanation
framing.note: KRONOS starts from the presumption of innocence. The line of inquiry and the alternates are tested against the same records; neither is a finding, and the strengths are not probabilities.

alternateHypotheses.title: Was near the scene for a routine reason
alternateHypotheses.statement: Vikram Singh was near the scene because they regularly go there (home, work, market), not because of the incident.
alternateHypotheses.label: Moderate

evidence.text: Recorded within 1 km of the scene on 42 other days (14 Apr – 10 Jun), so presence there is part of their routine

alternateHypotheses.test: Establish why the person is regularly there (address, employment, shop) and compare the incident-time visit with their usual pattern (time of day, duration).

alternateHypotheses.title: Named or given a role in error
alternateHypotheses.statement: Vikram Singh was named in the FIR, or assigned a role, without an independent basis.
alternateHypotheses.label: Moderate

evidence.text: FIR text contains: '…no role has been attributed…'

alternateHypotheses.test: Re-examine the FIR and statements; record the person's statement and the informant's basis for naming them.

alternateHypotheses.title: The money has a legitimate explanation
alternateHypotheses.statement: The flagged money movements of Vikram Singh have an ordinary purpose (salary, rent, property, business) or belong to a co-holder of the account.
alternateHypotheses.label: Moderate

evidence.text: Flagged NEFT ₹720,000 on 2025-05-13 22:47 has a stated purpose 'consultancy fee'

alternateHypotheses.test: Obtain full statements, invoices or agreements and KYC; confirm the stated purpose with the counter-party.

alternateHypotheses.title: Mistaken identity
alternateHypotheses.statement: Records belonging to someone else (a namesake or a wrongly matched profile) were attributed to Vikram Singh.
alternateHypotheses.label: Moderate

evidence.text: Identity match with P00035 has contradicting records

alternateHypotheses.test: Confirm identity with photograph or fingerprints (NAFIS), father's name and address from the FIR particulars.

alternateHypotheses.title: The contact was routine, not coordination
alternateHypotheses.statement: Vikram Singh's calls and messages reflect a long-standing relationship (family, work, business), not planning of the incident.
alternateHypotheses.label: Moderate

evidence.text: In contact with Jaspreet Mehta since 2025-04-14, 29 days before the incident (5 calls, 7 messages) — a long-standing relationship
In contact with Varun Bansal since 2025-04-14, 29 days before the incident (19 calls, 9 messages) — a long-standing relationship
In contact with Karan Dhillon since 2025-04-20, 23 days before the incident (3 calls, 6 messages) — a long-standing relationship

alternateHypotheses.test: Examine message content and the timing of contact relative to the incident; establish the relationship.

alternatesConsideredNotSupported.title: Someone else used the phone or handset

comparison.verdict: Every supporting item could be explained by at least one alternate, although the line of inquiry is stronger on weight (0.95 vs 0.58). Test the alternates before relying on it.
settleWith: A2 — Establish why the person is regularly there (address, employment, shop) and compare the incident-time visit with their usual pattern (time of day, duration).

hypotheses.hypothesis: Vikram Singh (P00036) was involved in the incident recorded in CASE032
hypotheses.name: Vikram Singh

supporting.text: record within 0.01 km of the incident location within 2 h of the incident
in contact with P00202 (12 contacts), P00054 (8 contacts)
Possible same person as P00035 (Ashok Sidhu), identity score 0.664 [PENDING, behavioural basis]

contradicting.text: FIR text contains: '…no role has been attributed…'
Identity match with P00035 has contradicting records

alternativeExplanations: An identity match may be wrong — similar names, shared family devices or accounts can belong to different people.
Being named in an FIR records an allegation; it is not itself proof of involvement.
Being near the incident place may be routine (home, work, market) — check whether the person regularly visits it.
Flagged transactions may have legitimate explanations (business payments, loans, property, salary) — verify documents.
Frequent contact may reflect family, business or social ties unrelated to the incident.

confidence.note: Evidential balance compares weighted supporting vs contradicting evidence; it is not a probability of guilt. Prior records are excluded from this score.

note: Each hypothesis is tested from both sides to reduce confirmation bias. Confidence scores are evidential balance (not probability of guilt). Human review is required.
